SR6105d83870a1e737.text: The central legal question is whether, prior to the 1929 enactment of Section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgagor in possession had the power to grant a permanent lease of the mortgaged property so as to bind the mortgagee.

SRc861336bccd1163c.text: Raja Nilkanth Narain Singh mortgaged Gadi Sirampur to the Chota Nagpur Banking Association Limited on 1st August, 1914. The Bank obtained a mortgage decree on 29th November, 1921, and purchased a third share on 28th October, 1922.

SRa7796579ce36c970.text: During the pendency of mortgage proceedings, on 5th November, 1925, Wazir Narain Singh granted a permanent lease of four villages to Hiraman Ram, Manager and Karta of his joint Hindu family, and his son Chohan Ram.
SRa7796579ce36c970.event: Permanent lease granted during mortgage suit pendency
SRa7796579ce36c970.procedure: Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh

SRb8df43a03806601b.text: An agreement was made that if Wazir Narain Singh paid Rs. 1,10,631-4-0 by 16th August, 1926, the sale would be set aside. He executed a mortgage on 14th August, 1926, to the Court of Wards to satisfy dues and set aside the sale.
SRb8df43a03806601b.event: Sale set aside and new mortgage executed

SRe56553556cf6a879.text: The Plaintiff (through the Manager of the Court of Wards) filed a suit on 4th February, 1929, to enforce the mortgage, impleading Hiraman Ram and Dilo Ram as co-defendants. A final decree for sale was passed on 18th September, 1931.

SR49a85ac37c355063.text: Dilo Ram died after the mortgage decree. Hiraman Ram and his son Chohan Ram continued in actual possession. The Plaintiff filed the suit on 16th November, 1939, against them for khas possession of the villages.
SR49a85ac37c355063.procedure: Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh

SR43b1f9b4f4974e70.text: Defendant 2 contended that the Plaintiff was not subrogated to the Bank's position, the decree was not binding as he was not a party, the Patta was not ended by the auction sale, and a partition occurred within a year allotting properties to him.

SR89feb810c247d711.text: The Trial Court held the Plaintiff was subrogated to the Bank's position, Defendant 1 was the Manager/Karta, Defendant 2 was fully represented, the decree was binding, and the Plaintiff was entitled to recover possession and mesne profits.
SR89feb810c247d711.procedure: Court of Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh

T7e999ac770b67863.SUPPORT: The central issue is whether a mortgagor in possession could grant a permanent lease binding on a subsequent mortgagee before Section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act came into force in 1929.

T5224ab3cb1ca9fe9.EXCEPTION: The trial court found the defendants were fully represented in the mortgage suit, making the decree binding, which the High Court later negated on res judicata grounds.
